correctness.rationale: Subspaces invariant under multiplication by t correspond to ideals of F_q[t] containing (f); the subspace (g)/(f) has codimension deg(g) in V. A subalgebra outside V has exactly q^deg(g) lifts of its intersection W=(g)/(f), because a normalized exterior generator is specified modulo W. All subspaces inside V are abelian, giving the Gaussian counts at codimension one higher. For ideals outside V, the necessary and sufficient condition is tV contained in W. Its codimension in V is zero or one as t does not divide or divides f, giving just the whole algebra or additionally q codimension-one ideals. Pairs in V have ordinary span dimension 0, 1 or 2 with the asserted rank counts. For fixed nonzero exterior coordinates (a,b), the combination av-bu is uniform over V with fiber size q^m and one exterior direction remains. An element w with annihilator (g) generates a cyclic module of dimension deg(g) and is (f/g)c with c a unit modulo g (g=1 gives the single zero element). This gives all N_j, the full-generation probability by division by q^{2m+2}, and the irreducible gap. The proof does not require squarefreeness or odd characteristic. A separate direct census at q=2, f=t^4+t^2, using coset subspace generation, bracket tests and poset inversion for generated dimensions, gives subalgebra, ideal and pair distributions (1,5,27,51,31,1), (1,3,2,3,2,1), and (1,93,306,240,192,192); replay: python3 /workspace/branches/independent_lie.py. originality.rationale: The coverage is by direct implication rather than an earlier located table carrying N_j. Avetisyan's Proposition 3 describes every subalgebra and ideal for arbitrary almost Abelian actions over any field. Its restriction to a cyclic module gives both zeta polynomials by counting lifts through each invariant subspace. For the full pair profile, not just the full-algebra probability, fix one normalized exterior linear combination of the two generators. By Proposition 3, the subalgebras containing that combination are indexed exactly by their invariant intersection W with V. Containing the other generator then means W contains av-bu. For each W=(f/g)/(f), apply Brent–Gao–Lauder's existing one-vector generating formula to W itself, which is cyclic with annihilator (g): exactly Phi_q(g) vectors there generate W (one for W=0). Summing over W of dimension j-1 and multiplying by (q^2-1)q^m, the elementary fiber count for the projection (u,v) to av-bu, gives the entire exterior term. The pairs in V are just ordinary matrix ranks. Thus all claimed components follow from the existing stronger descriptions by ordinary cyclic-submodule and vector-space counting, without a new case-specific mathematical step.
